observation.visible_scene: Extreme close-up with very shallow depth of field of a turntable. A black vinyl record rests on a brushed-metal platter occupying the lower-left of the frame. On the right, a tonearm terminates in a silver headshell (with two small screws) holding a black cartridge/stylus assembly that hovers above the deck, to the right of and clear of the record's edge; a thin arm tube extends off the right frame border. The background (turntable chassis and a blurred pivot/control area) is out of focus, and soft pinkish reflections glow on the metal surfaces.
visible_changes: The tonearm/headshell assembly undergoes a small, slow angular and positional drift across the segment: the arm tube leaving the right edge tilts slightly and the headshell shifts a little, but the cartridge never moves over the record and remains clear of the vinyl throughout.
A bright highlight on the left rim of the metallic platter changes subtly in shape and position between frames.
Overall framing stays largely steady, with only minor apparent movement of the scene/camera.
The record itself shows no obvious in-plane translation; its rim stays in the same place relative to the platter.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the tonearm is being lowered toward the record or lifted away, and whether the platter is rotating.
What occurs before the first frame and after the last (the segment is a temporal crop with arbitrary ends).
Whether the stylus ever contacts the record.
The cause of the small tonearm shift (manual handling, motorized movement, or camera motion).
uncertain_details: Whether the observed changes are tonearm object motion, slight camera motion, or a combination of both.
Whether the shifting platter highlight indicates actual platter/record rotation or just lighting/camera variation.
The exact direction and magnitude of the headshell drift; it is small and may be partly framing noise.
